title: 42a: upper bound 0.6863607950* on Bakeas's Theorem A (unrefereed)
body:
Records the unrefereed claim **C₄₂ ≤ 0.6863607950***, on top of #302, preserves historical bounds, and updates the README bound and recent progress.

This is Vasileios Bakeas's method, not a new construction. The limit theorem (Theorem A), the residual lemma and the phase construction are theirs (V. Bakeas, turan-c42-bound, 2026, version 1.1.0, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23836302), and they build on Harcos's and Biró's finite linearization. Their notes already report about 0.686361 as the floating optimum of this family, so this mostly certifies that value. Bakeas suggested filing it as a separate row after #302, so that each certificate stays with its author.

What's new here is the non-uniform grid (49 rational phases on knots j²/4608) and tighter error propagation: an integrated residual bound and a smaller kernel cap near 0. They bring the certificate to about 2e-8 of the claim. Theorem A is stated for knots j/48. Its proof uses only a finite piecewise-linear phase, with |d(u)| ≤ TΛu for Λ the largest slope, so it applies verbatim to these knots, as Bakeas confirmed. It also assumes Re γ ≥ 0; here a = 0.1118, and both programs check a > 0.

Certificate, verifiers, derivation and receipts: https://github.com/rpinho/c42-certificate/tree/009120a811abd6840a9417e9f1c02cd490c5f608/volterra-quadratic-knots. Two Arb verifiers pass, at F ≤ 0.6863607742 and F ≤ 0.6863607773. One is written from Bakeas's theorem and the other adapts their MIT-licensed independent checker. They're separate implementations, but they share the new propagation bounds, so those bounds have no independent implementation.

A separate AI review re-derived Theorem A and the new bounds, found no mathematical gap, and got F ≈ 0.68636074 from its own direct Volterra solve, which is a diagnostic and not a certificate. That is not a second party. Bakeas checked the bundle and found no error. They re-derived every new bound, read the first verifier line by line against the derivation, and read the diff of the adapted checker against their own. They didn't have the memory for the full N = 14,155,776 run. At N = 294,912 and 589,824 the verifier gave F ≤ 0.6864311 and F ≤ 0.6863783, unproved as expected, and h² scaling to the full N predicts F ≤ 0.68636077, which matches the receipts. A separate floating-point solver of theirs converges to F ≈ 0.686360744. They read the versions before one change: both programs now refuse to run under `python -O`, which Bakeas suggested, and all receipts were rerun afterwards. The asterisk stays.

No exhaustive priority or optimality is claimed. A wider search for anything below this family's optimum has found nothing so far.

title: 42a: improve the upper bound for Turán's pure power-sum constant to 0.68637* (phase-varying first block, τ = 0)
body:
This PR adds a [Bak26] row to the upper-bound table of `constants/42a.md`. It also adds the reference, a contribution note, and one comment pointing to certified finite-n bounds [Bak26b]. In `README.md` it updates the cell for 42 and adds a line to Recent progress. Markdown changes only.

**Claim.** C42 ≤ 0.68637* (previously 0.6873358063*, #263).

**Construction.** Harcos's linearization, which is exact for every n:
- prescribe s_k = T e^{iφ(k/n)} for k ≤ ⌊n/2⌋, with T = 0.68637 and a piecewise-linear phase φ (24 pieces);
- give the remaining power sums a common modulus F_n, chosen so that 1 is a root;
- hence R_n ≤ max(T, F_n).

Unlike the coefficient-cancellation certificates, the phase is not held constant on a first block (cut-off τ = 0).

**Proof.** The note (NOTES.md) proves F_n → F, where F is given by an explicit linear integral equation. The hypotheses are sup|d| = T < 1, which makes the relevant convolution operator a contraction, and Re γ ≥ 0. For a constant phase the formula reduces to Harcos's 0.693676.

**Verification.** Two independently written Arb checkers (python-flint 0.9.0) apply an a posteriori bound (Lemma 3 of the note) on a 122880-cell grid. They give F ≤ 0.6863660 and F ≤ 0.6863615, both < 0.68637:

    python rigorous_limit.py c42_profile_0.68637.json 2560
    python independent_check.py c42_profile_0.68637.json 2560

Two floating-point cross-checks give F ≈ 0.6863601:
- a direct solver of the limit equation;
- the exact finite-n construction, up to n = 4·10^6.

**Repository.** https://github.com/Bakeas/turan-c42-bound (tag v1.1.0, commit dc9c491ccb0a9ee8de753739eb082fa84c25c091). Archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23836302. Profile SHA-256: dcea4edbec1d5935f2f04d4d1b5b8379e2d2d7d78072a1f089c7abbe11ded395.

**History.** This PR first claimed 0.6865* (version 1.0.0, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23825118). Version 1.1.0 keeps the proof and changes only the profile. It also fixes a bug in the first checker found by Ricardo Pinho (a missing positivity check of the denominator bound); the bug did not affect the result.

**AI use.** Found and prepared with Claude (Anthropic; Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5) under my direction. A separate Claude agent reviewed the proof working from the note only (AI_REVIEW.md, versions 1.0.0 and 1.1.0), and wrote the second checker without access to the first. No human mathematician has checked the argument. Unrefereed; no explicit finite threshold is claimed. I have checked that all links and references in this PR open and point to the right material.

title: C59: improved upper bound K_2 < 0.302825279490988* (Bohr radius of the bidisc)
body:
Updates the upper bound for [C59](constants/59a.md), the Bohr radius $K_2$ of the bidisc, from 0.302825279492 (P2026, Patel) to 0.302825279490988.

**Size of the improvement: about 1.0e-12** (0.302825279492 - 0.302825279490988 = 1.012e-12). P2026's bound is exact (Lean theorem `bohrRadius_lt_302825279492_div_10pow12`), so this is a genuine but very small improvement.

### Construction

f(z, w) = A + B Δ (I - D Δ)^-1 C with Δ = diag(z, w) is the transfer function of an exactly unitary 3x3 colligation U = [[A, B], [C, D]] with Gaussian-rational entries over a common 149-digit denominator, so f is a Schur function on the bidisc (the n = m = 1 realization class contains P2026's witness). Exact integer arithmetic on the 1681 coefficients f_jk, 0 <= j,k <= 40, shows the finite Bohr majorant sum |f_jk| r^(j+k) is at least 1 + 2.2e-42 at r = 3028252794909880/10^16, hence K_2 < 0.302825279490988.

title: C44: upper bound 2.0417086280* with R4 = 22 and classification at small degree (unrefereed)
body:
Records the unrefereed claim **C₄₄ < 2.0417086280***, preserves historical bounds, and updates the README bound and recent progress.

This is a large move for an elementary argument, so please read it with suspicion. It replaces the 2.1974348818, 3.9819073803 and 4.1225323803 filed here, and rests on the 2.1974 argument described below. The lower bound is 1.5.

For a ternary polynomial of real degree at most k with support density p and h relevant coordinates, the support lemma and Fourier energy give h ≤ floor(k p 2^(k+1)). Applied to a Boolean derivative, fixing those control coordinates lowers the degree on every branch and leaves a signed dictator on the active ones. The Kasami-Tokura weight spectrum cuts the case analysis to finitely many exact cases, giving ceilings R₄ ≤ 24, R₅ ≤ 54, R₆ ≤ 119, R₇ ≤ 254, R₈ ≤ 528. The Chiarelli-Hatami-Saks identity turns these into local-weight caps for Wellens's recurrence. The block-sensitivity inputs are no longer active. R₃ ≤ 10 and the second Reed-Muller weight 3/2 are cited, not reproved.

The method is new to me, but the recursion is short enough that it may already exist, and related structure appears in Valyuzhenich (2023). No exhaustive priority or optimality is claimed, and I'd welcome a check.

Rounds on top of that argument add exact small-degree input: R₄ = 22, using the published cubic classification, then R₅ ≤ 50 and R₆ ≤ 109 by a 52-case classification and Boolean completion compatibility. **Construction.** The finite obstruction inequality on the page, with 54 primes.
- Base, 29 primes with orders dividing T₀ = 12252240 = 2⁴·3²·5·7·11·13·17: Yoo's 14 (3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19, 29, 31, 37, 41, 61, 73, 257), the 7 added in #281 (43, 127, 241, 113, 109, 97, 151), and **8191, 53, 157** (orders 13, 52, 52), **23, 89, 397, 683** (orders 11, 11, 44, 22), **137** (order 68).
- Clusters, 25 primes: Griego's and Yoo's clusters without orders 11 and 13: 23: 47, 178481 | 29: 233, 1103, 2089 | 37: 223 | 43: 431, 9719 | 47: 2351, 4513 | 53: 6361 | 73: 439 | 79: 2687 | 83: 167 | 113: 3391 | 131: 263 | 179: 359, 1433 | 191: 383 | 233: 1399 | 239: 479, 1913, 5737, 176383 | 251: 503.

Moving 8191, 23, 89 from their clusters into the base leaves the sum unchanged (the same CRT factorisation), but puts 13 and 11 into the base period, which makes primes of order 2p and 4p available. Measured gains: 53, 157 together 7.61e-5; 397 1.22e-5; 683, 137 together 2.61e-5. Exact sum S = 0.48948174348600104752999373053459010942…, 6.98e-4 below [Y2026] and 1.14e-4 below #281.

**Computation.** Grouping the base primes by the part of their order outside 12 splits r mod T₀ into r mod 12 and one private coordinate per group, so ν₀ = Σ_{c mod 12} ∏_G α_G(c) with independent factors; groups whose orders are prime to 3 see only r mod 4. Partial products are merged under the affine maps of Z/12 and Z/4, with 256-bit counts. For classes with ν₀ above C = 1538836 the term is 1/(2M) for every cluster multiplier, so the histogram keeps exact bins for ν₀ ≤ C (1,434,945 entries, sha256 e011429b8f49cd362db1f8a3273fe5ceeff97d1067af1e97bfbbdf2bddfaf91c) and one exact aggregate line (count, Σν₀, Σν₀²) for the rest; the verifier checks (C+1)·m_min ≥ thr. On the 51- and 52-prime sets this path reproduces the full histograms byte for byte without the cut, and with the cut gives the same bins up to C and the same count, Σν₀, Σν₀² above it. The 54-prime histogram takes about 1 h on 2 cores.

**Verification.**
- `./verify.sh --stored` checks the three stored histograms in about 20 seconds; `./verify.sh` rebuilds the 54-prime one from the residue conditions.
- The generator self-tests every mode against direct enumeration over a mod M₀ on small prime sets.
- The verifier checks the histogram's total and first two moments (aggregate included) against values computed directly from the residue conditions, independent of the generator; checks its pipeline against the bound computed from its definition on a small set and that a cut below the trivial regime is rejected; and evaluates S with Fractions and a rational λ < log 2.

title: C1c: exact extremal constant D0 = 1/(2(1+theta0)) via the ±π phase lock and the intrinsic-fracture factor
body:
This PR adds the exact determination of $C_{1c}$ to the constant page.

**What is added.** A new "Extremal constant" table sits between the Known upper bounds and Known lower bounds tables. It records the exact extremal constant

$$D_0 = \frac{1}{2(1+\theta_0)} = \frac{1}{2(1-\cos x^*)} = 0.410767488189405337670475533141972203071146700975983509368218\ldots$$

with $x^* = c\pi$, $c = x^*/\pi = 1.430296653124203\ldots$, pinched between $\pi$ and $3\pi/2$ and locked by the eigen-equation $\tan x = x$ ($x^*$ is the least positive solution of $\tan x = x$).

**Why this is the value.** The field's upper bound $1/(2(1+\theta_0)) = 0.4107675$ is the four-digit rounding of $D_0$ itself, so the upper side has already touched the value; the lower ladder ($0.4103287 \to 0.4103334 \to 0.4103433$) approaches from below. The notation $L\uparrow D \downarrow U = D_0$ records the two-sided convergence. The pinching is recomputed from the single input $\pi$ (Machin) plus the eigen-equation in finite rational arithmetic; see the verification script `constants/c1c_two_way_pinching.py` added in this PR.

**Relation to the field's record.** The exact form is [MR2020, (1.2)]; the dual test-function method cannot go below $D_0$ ([MR2020, Thm 4.1]: $\|(\hat\varphi)_+\|_1 \geq 1/(2(1+\theta_0))$); the only non-sharpness established in [MR2020] is within a restricted class of functions, non-quantitatively (Thm 1.7). None of these determines the extremal value; the $\pm\pi$ phase lock fixes $D_0$ as the value, with the intrinsic fracture $\delta = 6\Phi^2 - 5\pi = 9+3\sqrt5 - 5\pi = 5\varepsilon$ entering as a factor of the constant.

Details are in the preprint [S2026c] (Zenodo v1, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23694729), cited on the page.

body:
This PR adds one comment to 26a. **The lower bound 2 and the README cell are unchanged**, since all the new values
are below 2.

**Statement.** For every d ≥ 1 there is an explicit f_d : {±1}^{3d} → {0, ±1} of degree d with exactly (2^d − 1)·2^d
nonzero Fourier coefficients, all ±2^{−d}. Hence

BH^{≤d}_{±1} ≥ 2(1 − 2^{−d})^{(d+1)/(2d)},

which is larger than the address-function value 2^{(d−1)/d} for every d ≥ 2:

| d | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| new (truncated) | 1.61185 | 1.82965 | 1.92093 | 1.96226 | 1.98171 | 1.99105 |
| address | 1.41421 | 1.58740 | 1.68179 | 1.74110 | 1.78180 | 1.81145 |

**Construction.** f_d is a sum of 2^d − 1 codimension-d affine blocks χ_β·1_A, one for each proper subset J of ℤ_d.
They are built from a d-cycle on z₀…z_{d−1} and d pairs (aᵢ, bᵢ). The live sets are pairwise disjoint and the
Fourier cosets are pairwise disjoint, so f_d is {0, ±1}-valued with Pr[f_d ≠ 0] = 1 − 2^{−d}. The proof is about a
page. A two-line argument also shows that every {0, ±1}-valued f of degree d has ratio at most
2·Pr[f ≠ 0]^{(d+1)/(2d)} < 2, so this route cannot reach 2. That is consistent with the page's note that the
interesting direction is elsewhere.

title: 37a: no Boolean function of degree 4 has sensitivity 10 (comment only, no bound change)
body:
This PR adds one comment to 37a. **The bound log₃ 6 and the README cell are unchanged.**

**Statement.** No Boolean function of degree 4 has sensitivity 10: there is no q : {0,1}¹⁰ → {0,1} with deg q ≤ 4,
q(0) = 0 and q(eᵢ) = 1 for all i. So s(f) ≤ 9 for every f of degree ≤ 4, which is attained by NAE₃∘NAE₃.

**Why it matters for 37a.** Composition powers of a fully sensitive (n, d) function give C₃₇ ≥ log n / log d.
(10, 4) would have given log₄ 10 ≈ 1.661. It is the only degree-4 case above Kushilevitz that the symmetrisation LP
(Wellens 2022, Table 1) leaves open. Proskurin (arXiv:2101.08600, §5) singled it out, showing that its symmetrisation
would be unique, and left existence open. Maitra–Mukherjee–Stănică–Tang (DAM 2025) excluded only rotation-symmetric
functions. The LP relaxation of the problem is feasible (Proskurin's symmetric point), so the proof has to use
integrality.

title: Add C_89c: Ramsey multiplicity constant of K_6, with a certified upper bound 0.7422548616·2^-14 (was 0.7445·2^-14)
body:
**Stacked on #277** (the 89b page and README rows): this branch carries #277's commit underneath. Once #277 is merged, only the second commit remains.

Adds **C_89c, the Ramsey multiplicity constant of $K_6$**, with a **new certified upper bound** $C_{89c} \le 0.7422548616 \cdot 2^{-14}$*. The previous best is $0.7445 \cdot 2^{-14}$ (Franek, Combinatorica 2002, exactly $51162598917 \cdot 2^{-50}$; Deza–Franek–Liu 2012), so the new bound is 0.30% lower. Markdown only: `constants/89c.md`, a README row and a "Recent progress" line.

**Construction.** Franek's bound comes from blow-ups of the Cayley graph on $\mathbb{Z}_2^{10}$ with $x \sim y$ iff $\lvert x \triangle y\rvert \in \{1,3,4,7,8,10\}$ (red inside the blocks). Keeping all its symmetries, the red density between blocks $x, y$ becomes a free function of the Hamming weight $\lvert x \triangle y\rvert$: 11 numbers in $[0,1]$. L-BFGS-B from Franek's 0/1 point gives $(1, 0.43996, 0, 1, 1, 0.01295, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0.76253)$, which is rounded to multiples of $2^{-20}$.

**Exact evaluation.** Fixing $x_0 = 0$, the density is a sum over the $\binom{41}{10} \approx 1.1 \times 10^9$ multisets of column types of $(x_1, \ldots, x_5)$; all 15 pair weights are column counts. Two separately written C programs compute the integer numerator modulo 61-bit primes, combined by CRT (6 primes plus a check prime). One is a DFS with incremental weights; the other iterates over count vectors and recomputes everything per leaf, sharing no code. Both give exactly

$180244428715156181493112659521741405180580225001966676111887908798425648907356856409/3978585891278293137243057985174566720803649206378781739523711815145275976100267004264448 = 0.742254861593625\ldots \cdot 2^{-14}$,

and both reproduce Franek's $51162598917/2^{50}$ from his parameters. Data and checkers are at [JeetuSK0808/tao-constants-certificates@98b6ee3](https://github.com/JeetuSK0808/tao-constants-certificates/tree/98b6ee34e8f51f82be85517e4b7f0e7e7af393b8/c89c-k6-ramsey-multiplicity). The bound is asterisked as self-hosted.

**Lower bound.** No dedicated lower bound for $c_6$ is in the literature; flag algebras of the size used for $c_4, c_5$ are out of reach. The page records the averaging bound $1/\binom{252}{6}$ from $R(6,6) \le \binom{10}{5}$ and cites Conlon's general bounds. Better published bounds on $R(6,6)$ improve it only marginally, and I kept the classical one rather than pick between conflicting recent figures.

body:
**C68 ≥ 0.446** (lower bound; previous 0.432* [Pin2026], before that 0.4263 [Wik2026]).

Certificate, proof and checkers: [vidigoat/optimization-records @ 1a76f9d, `tao/certificates/c68`](https://github.com/vidigoat/optimization-records/tree/1a76f9dd053d51cce531b57b2ad5a68e3205ca75/tao/certificates/c68).

**What changed.** The argument keeps Wikström's moment-duality criterion and Pinho's coefficient step, and sharpens the geometric input:

1. **Flux (period) lemma** (`PROOF.md`, Lemma 2). For ω: Ann → 𝔻 holomorphic with ω(z₁) = 0 and |z₁| = |z₂| = r,
   `−log|ω(z₂)| ≥ G(z₂, z₁) + σ·sech²(A/2)`, where σ = sin²(πφ(r)), φ(r) = 1 + log(r)/w, w = −log c, A = π²/w.
   Single-valuedness of ω makes the circle flux of −log|ω| an integer; the fluxes of the Green potentials G(·, b) are −φ_b or 1 − φ_b, the harmonic part's flux is bounded by its boundary means, and a uniform lower bound on the annulus Green function (Lemma 1) turns the integrality constraint into the extra term.
2. **Half-diameter enclosing lemma** (Lemma 5): with the pairwise bound from (1), each circle's image lies in a hyperbolic disk of radius D/2, replacing hyperbolic Jung's D/2 + log(2/√3).

Together G(t) = (1 + √(1 + Ψ/(2σ(t))))/2 with Ψ = (1+q)²/(8q), q = e^{−A}.

**Certificate.** c = 223/500, R = 99/100, 8 exact rational atoms plus Lebesgue measure on [R, 1]; every k is covered (direct checks for k ≤ 5806 / k ≤ 1349, analytic tail arguments beyond). Minimum relative margins 6.99·10⁻⁶. A second certificate gives 8921/20000 = 0.44605; exploratory LPs put the limit of this framework at about 0.44607.

#216, #230 and #232 applied the CONTRIBUTING rule that the marker "is removed when that changes — when the paper is refereed and published, or when the argument is formalized or independently replayed." This PR offers that replay for the two C31 rows merged in #231, with no code shared with the claimant. Markdown only.

**What was replayed.** [J2026] runs Lueker's upper-bound method ([L2009], Theorem 3.3): an automaton $M_h$ over pairs of binary strings with history length $h$, a weight matrix $A_z$, and a positive vector $v$ with $A_z v \le \lambda v$, which gives $\gamma_2 \le 2\log(2z)/\log\lambda$. Lueker computed $h \le 8$; the two rows take $h = 9$ and $h = 10$.

| row | states (ours = [J2026]) | $z$ | our certified $\lambda$ | [J2026]'s $\lambda$ | our bound | printed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $h = 9$ | 51,425,006 | 0.3298 | $\le 0.364708361168896$ | 0.364708361184292 | $\gamma_2 \le 0.8251002730$ | $0.825101$ ✓ |
| $h = 10$ | 400,253,317 | 0.3376 | $\le 0.385532597279844$ | 0.385532705434511 | $\gamma_2 \le 0.8241195407$ | $0.824120$ ✓ |

Beside each certificate a certified **lower** bound on the spectral radius of $A_z$, $\rho \ge 0.364708361168863$ at $h = 9$ and $\rho \ge 0.385532597279807$ at $h = 10$ (the minimum ratio under downward rounding): no certificate for these automata can print a $\lambda$ below it, and both of [J2026]'s sit above it, by $1.5 \times 10^{-11}$ and $1.1 \times 10^{-7}$. Any positive vector certifies, so those are valid, less converged certificates, not errors; both printed bounds hold with room.

**How.** The automaton was written from [L2009] alone (the 2008 extended version, whose Figure 8 and Theorem 2 are the journal's Figure 7 and Theorem 3.3), twice: a Python reference in the standard library and a C builder, which share no code with each other or with [J2026] (its `src/` and `review/` were never fetched). **What was replayed.** The certificate `cert_n1200_A11.json` at rpinho/c86-trace-certificate commit `116a58f` (sha256 `722a287b74a9…`): a step measure $\mu$ on the cells of width $1/200$ (629 nonzero cells, support $[1/20, 1037/200]$) and eleven integer polynomials $Q$ with rational weights $b_Q$. | | condition | how | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | $d_i \ge 0$, edges increasing, support inside $[1/20, 1037/200]$ | exact | holds |
| E2 | each $Q$ primitive, irreducible over $\mathbb{Z}$, totally real; the $Q$ distinct | exact (integer roots and monic quadratic factors within the Mignotte bound; Sturm counts) | holds for all eleven |
| E3 | $\sum_Q b_Q \deg Q < m$ | exact | $0.82978\,m$ |
| E4 | $\int \log\lvert Q\rvert\,d\mu > 0$ for each $Q$ | closed form in $g(u) = u\ln\lvert u\rvert - u$ at the edges, roots enclosed to $2^{-80}$, outward rounding | every lower end $> 0$ (each $\approx 10^{-4}$) |

| E6 | $\int x\,d\mu / m$ equals the certificate's bound and is $\le 1.8117251$ | exact | $144938007612277893/79999999999994000 = 1.81172509515360954\ldots$ |

**What was not re-derived.** The extension of E5 from the support to $\mathbb{C}$ (the minimum principle), the resultant argument that makes $\mu/m$ arithmetic, and Smith's theorem [Smi24] — published mathematics, cited by the row and read, not re-proved. title: C_60: record the lower bounds 1/5 (Marshall) and 1/4 (Lean-formalized)
body:
## Summary

Two lower bounds for $C_{60}=\alpha_{\mathrm{Fav}}$, the Favard-length decay exponent of the four-corner Cantor set. The page currently records $1/6$ (Nazarov–Peres–Volberg).

1. **$\alpha_{\mathrm{Fav}}\ge 1/5$, by Caleb Marshall** ([arXiv:2509.02882](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.02882), v2, 12 August 2026). Theorem 1.2, restated as Theorem 8.3: $\mathrm{Fav}(\mathcal N_{4^{-N}}(K^\infty))\le C_u N^{-1/5+u}$ for every $u>0$. This has not been recorded here yet.
2. **$\alpha_{\mathrm{Fav}}\ge 1/4$**, from a Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization: https://github.com/CoolRmal/FavardLength at commit `65f19d4`, registered on the Palomar registry as [PALOMAR-2026-09-24-000001](https://palomar-registry.org/entry?id=PALOMAR-2026-09-24-000001&version=1). It proves $\mathrm{Fav}(K_n)\le C_a n^{-a}$ for every $a<1/4$.

## Credit, and the relation to Marshall's work

The $1/4$ proof is built on Marshall's. The formalized combinatorial dichotomy is an endpoint form of his marked-cylinder and packing construction (v2, section 7), which is what replaced NPV's $K^{2+o(1)}$ propagation by $K^{1+o(1)}$. What is added is analytic: a joint negative moment of the whole low-frequency product. Marshall's section 8.5 and his Future Directions identify a weighted low-frequency estimate as the missing input that would give $1/4-u$, and describe $1/5$ as a barrier for the methods there.

Two further points of attribution, both recorded on the page:

- The Fourier-analytic framework (normalized densities, Riesz products, exceptional directions) is Nazarov–Peres–Volberg's.
- **Version 1** of Marshall's preprint (2 September 2025) did assert $1/4$ for this set, in Remark 1.3 and section 3.5. **Version 2 withdraws that assertion**, saying the substitution that would yield $1/4-u$ "is not justified by our current methods". I have recorded the withdrawn claim in *Additional comments* so the history is visible rather than silently dropped.

## Verification

- Compared theorems: `favard_le_rpow_of_lt_quarter`, `one_quarter_le_decayExponent`, and `le_one_of_mem_admissibleExponents` / `decayExponent_le_one`. The last two reprove the known $\alpha_{\mathrm{Fav}}\le 1$ from an elementary $\mathrm{Fav}(K_n)\ge 1/(320n)$, which also shows the admissible set is bounded above, so $\alpha_{\mathrm{Fav}}$ is a genuine supremum. Nothing claims $1/4$ itself is admissible.
- `Challenge.lean` spells out $C_n$, $K_n$, $\pi_\theta$, projection length, $\mathrm{Fav}$ and $\alpha_{\mathrm{Fav}}$ from Mathlib alone, and matches the definition on this page.
- No `sorry` outside the Challenge's statement holes, no `native_decide`; the axioms are `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. CI runs Lean Comparator against the challenge file and is green at the cited commit.
- The $1/4$ is registered on the Palomar registry ([PALOMAR-2026-09-24-000001](https://palomar-registry.org/entry?id=PALOMAR-2026-09-24-000001&version=1)), whose mechanical check reran Comparator in a sandbox and replayed the proof through Lean's kernel and the independent NanoDa kernel. Neither bound is refereed. If you prefer to mark either row with the unverified asterisk, please do; I have not added one.

## Changes

- `constants/60a.md`: two new rows in *Known lower bounds*, a note in *Additional comments* about the withdrawn v1 claim, and `[Mar2026]` and `[Lin2026]` references.
- `README.md`: the $C_{60}$ lower-bound cell becomes $\frac{1}{4}$, plus two lines in *Recent progress*.

## AI use

The $1/4$ argument was developed and formalized with AI assistance under my direction; `formalization.yaml` in the repository records the models and the literature search behind the novelty claim. This pull request was prepared with assistance from Claude (claude-opus-5).

title: Improve C_3a lower bound to 1.21418 via two-temperature cyclic compression
body:
## Summary

This PR records the lower bound

$$
C_{3a}>1.21418.
$$

The construction introduces a two-temperature cyclic-quotient theorem: the difference family uses one Gibbs tilt while the sum-family upper bound is optimized with a separate tilt. For

$$
M=\langle4,5\rangle\cap[0,80],\quad
x=\frac{8149}{10000},\quad
y=\frac{42571}{50000},\quad
R=\frac{249293}{10000},
$$

exact rational reconstruction certifies

$$
1+\frac{\rho-\sigma}{\log R}
=1.214180896097785\ldots>1.21418.
$$

The proof and verification package is available here:

[Source repository](https://github.com/carson-olaf/c3a-two-temperature-bound) · [ZIP release asset](https://github.com/carson-olaf/c3a-two-temperature-bound/releases/download/v1.0.0/c3a_two_temperature_121418_submission_bundle.zip)

ZIP SHA-256: `8e84a693a41c8fe211b67bcdd3539691b35ba409e6d3a0910875925b4a2d4ffb`

- Adds the `1.21418` row to `constants/3a.md`. The value is certified by an explicit finite construction with a kernel-checked Lean 4 proof, registered as Palomar entry [PALOMAR-2026-10-29-000038 v1](https://palomar-registry.org/entry?id=PALOMAR-2026-10-29-000038&version=1).

I ran the complete `./reproduce.sh` workflow on macOS with Homebrew GMP:
